chapter: Brother Lorenzo Tio Jr. and his career
title: Lorenzo's tunes sold to Ellington and Bechet's debt to the family
summary: Tio says Lorenzo wrote Sophisticated Lady and Mood Indigo material, Harlem Hot Shot with Steve Lewis, and that Sidney Bechet drew on his uncle and father.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Oh, yes. I know Barney Bigard told me that he sold a lot of numbers to Ellington, or quite a few, anyway. Do you remember which numbers those were? Did he ever tell you which ones he sold? Later, Duke put his name on them, and then Barney put his name on, I think, Mood Indigo or something.

Mood Indigo was right. Well, that's what he made, he sold, a sophisticated lady was originally written by Lorenzo Keough, and that was written right here on Havana Street at 2404. That was before he went to New York. Then he had Mood Indigo and Mood Glow, and him and Steve Lewis, which I would like that they made a number of, uh, Lorenzo Teo and Steve Lewis, Harlem Hot Shot. You tell me it was a pretty hot number. That was the title of it? That was the title of it. Harlem Hot Shot. I never heard, I never know anything about it, but I heard some people say that it was played over the A.
Yeah. They might have changed the name of it too, you know, give it a different title.
They do that. Well, then there was, uh, Sidney Bishy. Oh yes. Sidney Bishy was also got a lot of ideas from my uncle and my father. Then he came up with my brother.
